question.text:
$x$ $-3$ $-2$ $-1$ $0$ $1$
$y$ $-7$ $-4$ $2$ $5$ $10$

The vector of coefficients of the line $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} = (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}, \]

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $\mathbf{y}$ in this context?
question.explanation:
$x$ $\color{blue}-3$ $\color{blue}-2$ $\color{blue}-1$ $\color{blue}0$ $\color{blue}1$
$y$ $\color{red}-7$ $\color{red}-4$ $\color{red}2$ $\color{red}5$ $\color{red}10$

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 1 & \color{blue}-2 \\ 1 & \color{blue}-1 \\ 1 & \color{blue}0 \\ 1 & \color{blue}1 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}-7 \\ \color{red}-4 \\ \color{red}2 \\ \color{red}5 \\ \color{red}10 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

question.text:
$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$y$ $6$ $4$ $3$ $1$ $-1$

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above.

Hint: You can use the fact that \[ (X^T \! X )^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad X^T \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix}13 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} &= (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \! \mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix}13 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -1.7 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have the line $y = 6 -1.7x.$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Least-Squares Regression Line in Context

question.text:
The height (in feet) and the average number of points scored per game (APG) of four players on a basketball team are shown in the following table.

Height $(x)$ $6$ $6.5$ $6.5$ $7$
APG $(y)$ $5$ $8$ $10$ $10$

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the average number of points scored per game by a player whose height is $6.45 \, \textrm{ft}?$

Hint: You can use the fact that \[ (X^T \! X )^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 84.75 & -13 \\ -13 & 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad X^T \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} 33 \\ 217\end{bmatrix}, \] where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 6.5 \\ 1 & 6.5 \\ 1 & 7 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 8 \\ 10 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} &= (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \! \mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &=\begin{bmatrix} 84.75 & -13 \\ -13 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 33 \\ 217 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -24.25 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have the line $y = -24.25+ 5x.$

Finally, to predict the average number of points scored per game by a player whose height is $6.45 \, \textrm{ft},$ we substitute $x=6.45$ into the equation of the line:

\begin{align*} y &=-24.25+ 5(6.45) \\[3pt] &=8 \end{align*}

So, according to the model, the average number of points scored per game by a player whose height is $6.45 \, \textrm{ft}$ will be $8$ points per game.

question.text:
A store collected data about its profits (in thousands of dollars) for the year's first five months. This data is shown below.

Month $(x)$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$
Profit $(y)$ $12$ $15$ $16$ $15$ $20$

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the profit in the $6$th month, assuming the trend continues?

Hint: You can use the fact that \[ (X^T \! X )^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad X^T \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} 78 \\ 250 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 12\\ 15 \\ 16\\ 15 \\ 20 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} &= (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \! \mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 78 \\ 250 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 10.8 \\ 1.6 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have the line $y = 10.8+ 1.6x.$

Finally, to predict the profit in the $6$th month, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

\begin{align*} y &=10.8+1.6(6) \\[3pt] &=20.4 \end{align*}

So, according to the model, the profit in the $6$th month will be $\$20\,400.$

Note: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result may be unreliable.

question.text:
A physics experiment consists of a small object moving along a straight line. The following table contains data collected on the distance traveled by the object (in inches) during the first five seconds.

Time $(x)$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$
Distance $(y)$ $8.6$ $13.1$ $24.6$ $28.1$ $38.6$

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what distance will the object cover after $6$ seconds, assuming the trend continues?

Hint: You can use the fact that \[ (X^T \! X )^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad X^T \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} 113 \\ 414 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 8.6\\ 13.1 \\ 24.6\\ 28.1 \\ 38.6 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} &= (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \! \mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 113 \\ 414 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 0.1 \\ 7.5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have the line $y = 0.1+ 7.5 x.$

Finally, to predict the distance the object will cover after $6$ seconds, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

\begin{align*} y &=0.1+7.5(6) \\[3pt] &= 45.1 \end{align*}

So, according to the model, the object will cover a distance of $45.1$ inches in $6$ seconds.

Note: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result may be unreliable.

Hint: You can use the fact that \[ (X^T \! X )^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 15 & -5 \\ -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad X^T \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} 11.8 \\ 35 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1.2\\ 2.5 \\ 3.6\\ 4.5 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} &= (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \! \mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix} 15 & -5 \\ -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 11.8 \\ 35 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 0.2 \\ 1.1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have the line $y = 0.2+ 1.1x.$

Finally, to predict the height after $8$ years, we substitute $x=8$ into the equation of the line:

\begin{align*} y &=0.2+ 1.1(8) \\[3pt] &=9 \end{align*}

So, according to the model, the height of a pine tree that is $8$ years old will be $9$ feet.

Note: Since we're extrapolating ($x=8$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result may be unreliable.

example.title: Finding a Least-Squares Regression Line in Context

question.text:
A small business collected data on the number of hours of telephone usage and the total amount (in hundreds of dollars) of the company's weekly operating expenses. This data is shown below.

Hours $(x)$ $2$ $2.4$ $2.8$ $3.2$ $3.6$
Expenses $(y)$ $4$ $5$ $6$ $7$ $8$

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the company's weekly operating expenses if the telephone is used for a total of $4$ hours per week, assuming the trend continues?

Hint: You can use the fact that \[ (X^T \! X )^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{8} \begin{bmatrix} 40.8 & -14 \\ -14 & 5 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad X^T \mathbf{y} = \begin{bmatrix} 30 \\ 88 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
question.explanation:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2.4 \\ 1 & 2.8 \\ 1 & 3.2 \\ 1 & 3.6 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 5 \\ 6\\ 7 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

\[ X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and

\[ {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}. \]

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} &= (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \! \mathbf{y} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{8} \begin{bmatrix} 40.8 & -14 \\ -14 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 30 \\ 88 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2.5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have the line $y = -1+ 2.5x.$

Finally, to predict the amount of the company's weekly operating expenses if the telephone is used for a total of $4$ hours, we substitute $x=4$ into the equation of the line:

\begin{align*} y &=-1+2.5(4) \\[3pt] &=9 \end{align*}

So, according to the model, the company's weekly operating expenses will be $\$900.$

Note: Since we're extrapolating ($x=4$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result may be unreliable.
